title: HINT for Data Analysts — metrics keep one meaning
metaDescription: Keep metric definitions, grains, sources, formulas and caveats beside analytics work so assistants query declared data instead of guessing.
h1: Your assistant writes SQL fast. HINT keeps every metric on its definition.
intro: HINT keeps metric definitions, data grain, source columns and caveats in plain-text notes beside dashboards and queries. Your assistant reads the context for this domain before changing a number.

situations.before: Two dashboards use the same metric name with different filters.
situations.body: The formula, grain, exclusions and owner travel together into every scoped task.

situations.before: A query references a plausible column that is not in the source.
situations.body: Unknown fields become schema questions instead of silently broken joins.

situations.before: A fresh-looking chart hides stale or partial data.
situations.body: Freshness, quality limits and interpretation notes arrive beside the metric rather than in a forgotten wiki page.

example.intro: The Dunder Mifflin BI demo grounds the sales metric in an approved source.
example.after: It uses the metric's declared source and definition, checks referenced columns, and carries caveats into the answer.
example.compiled:
<metric name="sales-1">
  Approved metric grounded in SRC-1.
</metric>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent data, columns, freshness or metric definitions.
Change a metric's grain or exclusions without a decision.
Present an estimate without its caveat and source.
disclaimer: HINT keeps analytic definitions visible; data quality, access control and interpretation still require your organization's checks.

faq.q: Does this replace dbt or LookML?
faq.a: No. It supplies intent and constraints to assistants working with those systems and can point to their definitions as sources.
It can require declared sources and checks, but execution and warehouse validation remain in your analytics stack.

faq.q: Can different domains define different metrics?
faq.a: Yes. Folder scope separates domain-specific definitions while shared policies can sit above them.

keywordDescriptions.metric: Defines a measure, formula, grain and owner.
keywordDescriptions.dimension: Names an approved axis for grouping or filtering.
keywordDescriptions.grain: States what one row or observation represents.
keywordDescriptions.source: Identifies the table, file or governed evidence behind data.
keywordDescriptions.table: Describes an allowed table and its analytic role.
keywordDescriptions.formula: Records the exact calculation for a metric.
keywordDescriptions.filter: Sets an approved inclusion or exclusion rule.
keywordDescriptions.freshness: States how current the source must be.
keywordDescriptions.dashboard: Sets the audience and purpose of a BI surface.
